attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded to #ffffff on var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The text is invisible there, failing WCAG 1.4.3 contrast. The badge only works in dark theme.
attacks.evidence: .embargo { ... background: var(--surface); color: #ffffff; ... } and tokens.css light theme: --surface: #ffffff;

attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a span with only an onClick handler. It has no tabIndex, role, or keyboard handler, so keyboard-only editors cannot reach or activate it (WCAG 2.1.1). Its only child is an aria-hidden icon with no aria-label or visually hidden text, so it has no accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2, 1.1.1). The .unpublish class has :hover but no :focus-visible style, so focus would be invisible even if the span became focusable (WCAG 2.4.7).

handleUnpublish has no error handling and no pending state. If onUnpublish rejects, the rejection is unhandled and the editor gets no feedback on a destructive action. Repeated clicks during the await can open multiple confirm dialogs or send duplicate unpublish requests.
attacks.evidence: async function handleUnpublish(e) { ... if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id); }

attacks.claim: The unpublish action is shown on every published row, and the only guard in the diff is a client-side confirm. The diff does not show a server-side permission check or audit logging for taking a live story down. These may exist outside the diff, but the artifact does not show them.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side authorization and audit logging for the endpoint behind onUnpublish(draft.id); {draft.status === "published" && (<span className={styles.unpublish} ...)

attacks.claim: A trash icon is used for unpublish. Trash conventionally means delete, but the story is only removed from the site and returned to drafts. The icon misleads about the action's effect, though the confirm dialog follows.
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> on the unpublish control; confirm body: "will be removed from the site and returned to drafts."

attacks.claim: The newsroom-timezone requirement depends on formatInNewsroomTz, which is not in the diff. Whether embargoUntil is parsed as an absolute instant and rendered in the newsroom zone is unverified, and the badge shows no timezone label.
attacks.evidence: import { formatInNewsroomTz } from "../lib/time"; Embargo until {formatInNewsroomTz(draft.embargoUntil!, "MMM d, HH:mm")} (no zone label; helper implementation ABSENT)

attacks.claim: Embargo state is computed from the browser clock, so a skewed client can show the wrong embargo state. The non-null assertion and the unguarded formatter could also throw on a malformed timestamp and break the whole queue render.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date(); formatInNewsroomTz(draft.embargoUntil!, ...)

attacks.claim: In dark theme, the hover color --danger is not overridden and stays #b91c1c. Against the dark --surface-hover it is roughly 2.4:1, below the 3:1 non-text contrast expected for indicating the control's state.
attacks.evidence: [data-theme="dark"] block defines --warn and surface tokens but not --danger; .unpublish:hover { color: var(--danger); background: var(--surface-hover); }

attacks.claim: No tests cover the embargo predicate (null, past, future, invalid dates) or the unpublish flow, including the failure and double-click paths.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any test file changes in the diff
